dict.string: Just the page: the button pad disappears and the whole screen becomes three big targets — tap left to page back, right to page forward, above the page for power. A three-finger tap on the page toggles it too.
CrossPoint holds the screen on while you read. Turn these off to keep it awake instead — useful propped on a stand, where the screen dimming mid-page is the interruption.
Allow Device to Sleep on Battery
Allow Device to Sleep While Charging

TAKES EFFECT NEXT LAUNCH. Close CrossPoint from the app switcher and open it again; nothing changes until you do. This is the one setting here that cannot be applied live — the factor sizes the page buffer and picks which set of glyph bitmaps is loaded, and both are fixed before the first page is drawn.
How finely the page is drawn, as page pixels per e-ink pixel. Layout never moves: the same words break in the same places at every setting. Only the sharpness of the drawing changes.
Fine (3x) is what the app has always used, and gives the most detailed letterforms. It is larger than the screen, so the page is scaled down to fit and smoothed on the way.
Exact (2x) lands one page pixel on one screen pixel on this phone — no scaling and no smoothing at all. Letterforms are slightly coarser than Fine but nothing is resampled.
Panel (1x) draws exactly what the e-ink hardware draws, pixel for pixel, then enlarges it. Blocky by design: it is for comparing against the real device, not for reading.

array.string: Exact (2x) — one page pixel per screen pixel

dict.string:
The two colors the page is drawn in: the ink a black pixel becomes and the paper a white one becomes. Every gray in between is mixed from the pair, so the page keeps its shading whatever you choose. Each option sets a light and a dark version; the app follows the system appearance.
Default is what the app has always drawn — a soft black on warm white, measured from an e-ink panel. High Contrast is pure black on pure white. Sepia and Cool Gray warm and cool the page without losing contrast (10.2:1 and 13.2:1; the default is 13.3:1).
Choose Custom to type your own, in the four fields below. They keep whatever you last entered, so a detour through a preset loses nothing.

array.string: Off — the page holds its brightness
15 s — dims as you settle into a page
Readable — stops while you can still read it
Dim — past readable, plainly still there
Ghost — the shape of the page, not the words
Off — the page arrives at once
17 ms — 60 Hz, a real field sweep
300 ms — a wipe, not a tube
Subtle — the raster at a glance

Experimental: reads the open book aloud in your Spoken Content voice, turning pages as it goes. Tap a word to start reading from it, or tap the word being read to stop. With VoiceOver on, a two-finger double tap pauses and resumes. Reading continues with the screen locked. Turning it on takes effect at the next page turn.
Speaking rate is a percentage of normal. The Spoken Content rate slider in Accessibility settings does not apply here, so this is the one that moves it.
